newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council welcomes arrest of Rwanda suspects.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council welcomes arrest of Rwanda suspects.

text.p: Security Council members on Friday welcomed the recent arrest in Kenya of a number of people indicted by the U.N. Rwanda war crimes tribunal and thanked the Kenyan government for its cooperation.

In a statement to reporters after private council consultation, council president Peter Osvald of Sweden said: "Members of the council welcomed the arrest in Kenya of persons indicted by the criminal tribunal for Rwanda and thank the government of Kenya for their cooperation. Members of the council expressed full support for the work of the tribunal."

Seven suspects, including Rwanda's prime minister during the 1994 genocide, Jean Kambanda, were arrested in Nairobi on July 18. This week a Belgian alleged to have incited violence over Radio Mille Collines during the slaughter of up to a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus was also seized in the Kenyan capital.
